The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.

CBC News Podcasts is looking for an Associate Producer with expertise in podcast editing and sound design, and a passion for CBC’s news storytelling. This work supports the CBC News Podcasting strategy, which exists to reach new audiences for CBC’s journalism in the podcast and digital audio space.

This is a 12 month temporary, full-time position, Monday to Friday, primarily daytime hours but with flexibility for working with team members coast-to-coast. It is a hybrid role, requiring you to be in the workplace at least three days a week, at any of CBC locations in Canada. 

About CBC News Podcasts

Canada’s best journalism, on demand and delivered directly into your earholes.

Our mandate is to amplify our news journalism in the podcast space, and that means video and social media are key to our podcasting strategy.

We work with CBC teams in several ways;  

  • producing original always-on news podcasts like Front Burner and Two Blocks from the White House 

  • supporting our local This Is podcasts 

  • assisting network audio and video teams to increase their podcasting presence

  • developing original news podcast series like See You In Court and upcoming investigative series. 

We work in deep collaboration with CBC News Studios, the Podcast Audience Growth Hub, and CBC Podcasts to create audience-focused podcast content and best practices around podcasting.

About the Role:

In this role, you will support our news podcast teams, assigned to new and ongoing projects throughout the year as needed. 

This means you’ll be working with CBC journalists with varying levels of longform audio experience to help us amplify CBC’s original, enterprise and investigative content in the podcast space for new audiences.

You will be responsible for leading the recording and post-production for all audio projects, to ensure the highest quality sound. This includes booking studios, recording interviews and troubleshooting technical issues with software/audio equipment, as well as working with producers to edit and mix podcast episodes, source music, archival tape and clips, suggest edits and respond to edit notes.

You are equally comfortable behind the board in studio, or using software to mix a multi-track audio documentary. You believe high quality audio is important, love using sound and music to elevate audio storytelling, and are excited to share your knowledge and experience with colleagues at different stages of their podcasting journey.

 

You’re responsible for a variety of tasks, including but not limited to:

  • With oversight from a CBC News Podcasts Exec or Senior Producer, contribute to the development and production of CBC News Podcast projects as needed 

  • Support CBC News teams in building podcast content from their original, enterprise and investigative journalism

  • Coordinate and execute the recording and production of interviews for a podcast format

  • Mix and edit podcast episodes, promos, trailers and other audio assets, in coordination with the producer and senior producer

  • Source clips, archival tape, music, and sound for podcast projects

  • Manage all audio files associated with the podcast, for current and future use

  • Help to equip and guide journalists on best practices for recording audio in the field

  • Edit and mix episodes in accordance with CBC News Podcasts’ strategy and in adherence to the JSP

  • Coordinate and execute publishing of podcast episodes and metadata..

About You:

  • You are committed to CBC News’ values around local service, audio strategy, and our Journalistic Standards and Practices

  • You have a track record of recording studio interviews, mixing and editing long form audio and news format programs 

  • You have a minimum of 3 years experience in audio or podcast production

  • You have experience working with creative contributors,  responding to feedback and helping develop a podcast’s sonic footprint

  • You’re a sound expert who is stays on top of new techniques, processes and software in the audio spaceYou’re a critical thinker who can come up with innovative ways to use resources to support a wide variety of needs and possible use cases

  • You’re detail-oriented and love to nerd out what small tweaks can make big impacts on content, workflow and audiences 

  • You forge positive team relationships where you value collaboration, transparency, respect and inclusiveness

  • You understand the fundamentals of what makes a podcast different from our other news formats.

Does this sound interesting to you? Please apply with a cover letter that explains why this role with CBC News Podcasts is a fit for you, and include your podcasting CV.

Associate Producer TV (English Services) (On-Site)

CBC Saskatchewan is looking for an Associate Producer assigned to our live streaming and supper hour television programming based in Regina. 

As we know, audiences continue to evolve in how, where and when they engage with our content. We know now more than ever how important visual storytelling is for our journalism to reach current and new audiences and to ensure we stay relevant. We need to be live when audiences need us and on demand when audiences want us.

The successful candidate will be responsible for proposing original story ideas, developing program content, organizing interviews, doing research, as well as video editing and bringing the show to air. With appropriate direction, this role organizes and contributes to the preparation, production, post-production work for live and on demand video. Your platform delivery list includes CBC Saskatchewan’s FAST Channel, YouTube, TikTok, cbc.ca, and television – you know how to tailor your storytelling to each of these platforms and their audiences. 

While work is generally performed following established standards and procedures, there is a regular requirement for independent judgment and initiative.

This role requires a keen eye and a passion for paying attention to details. It is also important to have a strong sense of visual elements beyond traditional videos, such as infographics and value-added graphics. Work sometimes involves the coordination of the activities of others. 

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

- Demonstrated ability to work with a team, you may occasionally be leading your workgroup.

- Strong writing and editorial abilities.

- Strong and enthusiastic team player.

- Connected to the community we serve.

- Passionate about Saskatchewan, stories and issues.

- Curious, quick thinking, incisive and critical thinker.

- Innovative with programming ideas.

- Knowledge of television programming and in production for news and information programs including a demonstrated ability to write, edit (Avid), vet and line-up.

- Experience using programs such as iNews, Dalet, Avid would be considered an asset.

- Skilled using social media to research/ source stories; and as a breaking news tool.

- Experience in graphic design/editing would be an asset.

- Demonstrated attention to accuracy under time constraints required.

- University degree or equivalent, with a minimum of two years in a similar position preferred.

- Chase guests for interviews under tight deadlines.

Radio-Canada’s Community Experiences and Partnerships team in Québec city is looking for an energetic Communications Officer. This permanent position will be based in Quebec City.


Your Role


Reporting to the Manager, Community Experiences, you will be responsible for developing, co-ordinating and executing brand activations and events. Your goal is to elevate the Radio-Canada brand, maximize its reach and strengthen its community presence while deepening the connection between Canadians and their public broadcaster.


Key Tasks:

  • Develop, plan and deliver original brand activations and experiential events across the Quebec region.
  • Help negotiate, draft, monitor and implement partnership agreements.
  • Implement and co-ordinate internal/external communications strategies to ensure maximum visibility for all initiatives.
  • Draft clear strategic marketing briefs for stakeholders and work collaboratively with various communications teams (integrated strategy, creative studio, etc.).
  • Assist in designing brand activations aligned with marketing goals as well as developing and rolling out both small-scale initiatives and major events.
  • Help plan event calendars and production schedules, co-ordinate all steps involved, scout locations and manage budgets.
  • Oversee contests tied to partnerships, including drafting web and social copy, writing contest rules, obtaining legal approvals, sourcing and negotiating prizes, managing promotional visibility, and following up with winners and suppliers.
  • Assist the media relations team in drafting and distributing news releases.
  • Work with programming and technical teams to plan and execute remote broadcasts linked to community activities and partnerships.
  • Co-ordinate brand ambassadors during partnership and community experience activities, providing them training, guidance and ongoing support.
  • Collaborate on performance evaluations for implemented activities and campaigns, conduct post-mortems and optimize results.
  • Manage and respond to inquiries sent to the partnerships email account.
  • Support event and cultural engagement operations as needed.

This position is a combination of remote work and in-office presence. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers according to guidelines established by the sector.


What You Bring:


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in communications, advertising, marketing or a related field.
  • Three (3) years’ experience in a similar role.

Skills:

  • Knowledge of CBC/Radio-Canada, its mandate and its programming.
  • Demonstrated negotiation, planning and organizational skills.
  • A genuine passion for event management, with the flexibility to adapt to the unique schedule and demands of event work.
  • Leadership, self-direction, sound judgment and initiative.
  • Ability to thrive under pressure and manage multiple projects concurrently.
  • High level of creativity in designing promotional events and brand activations.
  • Creative, solutions-oriented team player with the ability to meet tight deadlines.
  • Proficiency with project management tools (e.g., Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Jira, Canva) and any other relevant software.
  • Exceptional writing and editing skills.
  • Good knowledge of the creative community in the Quebec region.
  • Experience with and strong grasp of marketing principles and brand-building strategies.
  • Flexibility to work irregular hours or extended shifts as required by the event schedule.
  • Valid Class 5 driver’s licence.

Shortlisted candidates will be tested as follows:

  • Practical test.
  • An interview.

  • Eye for detail and a creative thinker.

  • Flexibility in work hours as operations demand, including the ability to work shift work, including evenings, weekends and holidays, is required.

CBC News is seeking an experienced, thoughtful journalist to serve as our Middle East Correspondent, to lead our on-the-ground coverage of a region defined by far-reaching complexity, history, and global impact.

In the Middle East conflict and shifting peace agreements continue to affect the lives of millions, while reshaping the global economy and alliances. In this role, you will go beyond the immediate news cycle to bring nuanced, contextualized storytelling to life — illuminating human experiences, geopolitical realities, and the diverse perspectives shaping the region. 

The successful candidate will be an exceptional journalist, with a broad range of social media, video, audio and text storytelling skills aimed at mobile and streaming audiences. You bring a deep knowledge of  the Middle East - its history, its politics, its economics and how this all ties into Canada's shifting role on the global stage. 

You thrive in a demanding daily news environment meeting multiple deadlines. You understand how stories work across platforms and on any given day you could be filing to one or more platforms including social and digital, video and audio.  You are adept at delivering live analysis and context, often on short notice, just as easily as you’re able to deliver social-first video and packaged reports. All of your journalism adheres to the CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices. 

In this position, you will work closely with a video producer based in Jerusalem, as well as colleagues from Radio-Canada also working in the bureau. You will be supported by the World News team in Toronto, including the Senior Producer who will assign Middle East coverage. The minimum assignment length for this position is two years and, if agreed to by both parties, may be extended for up to an additional two years. 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Generate and execute compelling journalism that explores a variety of voices and perspectives, from daily news to short- and long-form features.

  • Go live on any platform whenever a story requires it.

  • Produce original content while also responding to breaking news and emerging stories in a fast-paced environment.

  • Pitch and cover stories that resonate with our national audience, with an ability to find the significance in world events for a Canadian audience.

  • Research and analyze complex issues using specialized sources to ensure our audience gets a deep, nuanced understanding of important topics.

  • Quickly identify significant issues and respond strategically to ensure they are covered accurately and effectively.

  • Develop and maintain a strong network of contacts with a wide range of sources.

What is required: 

  • You are a journalist with a minimum of 8 years of comparable experience, including significant reporting experience at a network/national level.

  • Your extensive experience demonstrates that you can pivot quickly when a story changes, you remain respectful to colleagues when there are competing deadlines and content demands, and be open to social-centric presenting / hosting.

  • Exceptional storytelling skills, with a proven ability to produce memorable social, written, audio and visual content

  • Exceptional critical thinking skills, with an ability to breakdown complex issues and explain them clearly to audiences

  • Demonstrated ability to produce compelling social video content.

  • Strong on-air presence and skill with live reporting.

  • Extensive knowledge of world news and current affairs issues

  • A collaborative team player with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and willingness to work long and flexible hours, including overtime, evenings and weekends as needed.

  • Excellent interpersonal skills combined with a successful track record of working as part of a small team

  • Strong grasp of CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices, with an ability to understand how they apply in your daily storytelling.

  • A university degree in journalism or an equivalent combination of education and experience is preferred.

Application Requirements

To be considered for this role, please provide links to your portfolio that include at least:  

  • Two (2) social media stories

  • Two (2) examples of packaged stories for broadcast (audio and visual)

  • Two (2)  examples of live breaking news coverage

  • Two (2) text stories 

  • Cover letter, that will be used, in part to evaluate written communication. 

  • Current CV

Please, do not use generative AI in your work samples or cover letter unless, of course, your work example is a story about AI. Consult these guidelines for helpful tips on how to apply, know what’s the process, and how to put your best foot forward.

Your Role


Radio-Canada News is seeking an experienced Cross-Platform Managing Editor to lead our investigative journalism and high-impact content unit, as well as the Décrypteurs fact-checking team.


To succeed in this role, you bring deep experience in investigative journalism, a comprehensive understanding of CBC/Radio-Canada’s Journalistic Standards and Practices (JSP) and exceptional editorial judgment.


Reporting to the Senior Director, Investigative Reporting and Original Content, you will oversee complex investigative projects while ensuring strict adherence to our JSP. You will leverage your creativity and insight into modern newsgathering to generate original, innovative story ideas that elevate the quality and impact of Les Décrypteurs and our investigative reporting across all platforms.


You will provide inspiring leadership while maintaining respectful relationships with team members, Legal Services and management in accordance with corporate workplace health and safety policies. You will also manage day-to-day team administration and build strategic partnerships with CBC investigative units to amplify our content nationwide. 


Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Lead and inspire a team of seasoned journalists.
  • Oversee cross-platform news production (television, radio and digital) from initial concept through to final publication and broadcast.
  • Supervise investigative reporting, co-ordinating coverage across both CBC and Radio-Canada networks.
  • Drive cross-departmental collaboration, serving as the primary liaison between editorial staff, investigative journalists, fact-checkers and Legal Services in Quebec and across Canada.
  • Track current events and emerging trends to identify strategic coverage opportunities.
  • Uphold editorial rigour via fact-checking, while expanding content reach through partnerships with international newsrooms.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

What You Bring:

  • University degree in journalism or a related field.
  • Minimum ten (10) years’ journalism experience.
  • Team management experience.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of journalistic processes, newsgathering methods and cross-platform news content production (TV, radio and digital).
  • Expertise in producing investigative stories.
  • Exceptional editorial judgment and thorough understanding of CBC/Radio-Canada’s Journalistic Standards and Practices (see our website).
  • Outstanding writing and storytelling ability.
  • Extensive knowledge of current events and strong analytical skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
  • Creative, innovative mindset.
  • Ability to thrive under pressure and manage multiple developing stories simultaneously.
  • Ability to work independently and proactively anticipate news trends.
  • Excellent command of French (working language).

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

Role

Provide technical support to users regarding IT and office automation operations, ensuring the smooth operation and monitoring of computer networks, peripherals and software, as well as the management of telecommunications and IT networks. The ultimate goal is to maintain data processing capabilities as well as the availability of all IT systems and office automation software.

Description of Duties

  • Respond to user difficulties (via phone or other communication channels) by conducting research, diagnostics and analysis to determine the nature of IT system problems; take necessary action based on priority to resolve issues and ensure the continuity of data processing, or escalate the problem when necessary; document in detail the circumstances and actions taken during your shift.
  • Work closely with users and the system maintenance and support teams to resolve operational issues by providing relevant information and documentation.
  • Ensure the recovery and integrity of files stored on drives, tapes or other media following operational problems, applying the established procedures; ensure the availability and integrity of source programs, software, etc., to successfully restore operational systems.
  • Write command files based on gathered information to resolve specific operational problems or enhance operational monitoring; prepare or edit necessary documentation for the use of these files.
  • Monitor the operation and performance of equipment, including computers, telecommunications/IT links, drives and other peripherals; contact vendors promptly in the event of a malfunction to arrange repair or replacement.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; prepare the necessary correspondence and reports based on available information, following up as required.
  • Familiarize other people with their job by explaining your own duties.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • You have a degree in computer science or a related field.
  • You have at least two years of experience providing on-site or telephone IT support.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?


If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!


Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities  connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.


You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.


When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.


We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency with Xcode, Git, and the Swift language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on the App Store.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVC, MVP, or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of SwiftUI, Combine.
  • Knowledge of AVPlayer, CoreData, and AlamoFire is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Cocoapods (including the design/maintenance of internal pods).
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.


Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

This role is a hybrid work arrangement. Work schedule to be discussed with the Hiring Manager according to the guidelines defined by the department.

Your role:

 

CBC’s Business & Rights team has two positions available: one in B&R Scripted, reporting to the B&R Senior Director, Scripted & Acquired, and the other in B&R Unscripted, reporting to the B&R Senior Director, Unscripted. 

As the Manager, Business & Rights, you work closely with the independent production community and are responsible for negotiating and drafting development and/or licensing agreements and business recommendations. You decide how to approach negotiations and structure deals that meet CBC’s rights and financing strategies and priorities. In addition, you have the ability to efficiently assess proposed project budgets and calculate the appropriate level of CBC and third-party funding to be included within the financing structure. You will make recommendations and seek approvals from your B&R Senior Director on deal terms that best represent CBC’s priorities and interests. As a Manager, Business & Rights, you will also manage the creation of streamlined (and nuanced) contracts that represent and protect CBC's position. 

For the Scripted Role: Your portfolio could include development, production and/or acquisition deals across scripted genres including kids, comedy and drama including scripted feature films. Experience working on productions governed by the CMPA’s Independent Production Agreements (WGC, ACTRA & DGC) would be considered an asset.

For the Unscripted Role: Your portfolio could include development and production deals for documentaries (shorts, one-offs, and series), factual entertainment, award shows and variety shows.  Knowledge of music rights, and experience working with documentaries, format based factual entertainment, competition and event/concert shows, would be considered an asset 

Your project portfolio is expected to be diverse and could include development agreements, feature film licensing agreements and complex acquisitions, in addition to licensing agreements for original Canadian productions. Your responsibilities would include:

  • Taking a tailored approach to deal and contract negotiations for a wide range of projects including big budget scripted series intended for CBC’s platforms including but not limited to primetime television, CBC Gem, CBC FAST Channels and YouTube.

  • Ensuring CBC's contractual requirements and business interests are secured on a consistent and nuanced basis across programs of similar scope.

  • Reviewing and recommending third-party financing sources for each project with a critical eye to ensure eligibility and compliance with oft-changing requirements.

  • Reviewing third party agreements, including agreements from public and private funding agencies, and deals with other Canadian and international media platforms to ensure harmonization with CBC’s rights.

  • Applying strategic thinking to funding agency applications, to maximize benefits while ensuring CBC is accurately and strategically represented.  

  • Assisting in research, management and presentation of rights data across genres, platforms, and windows of exploitation.

  • Refining our business approach through continuous innovation, agile processes, and market-leading thinking about rights and financing models.

  • Authorizing contract payments where required. 

We are looking for candidates with the following: 

  • A post-secondary education or related experience, with a strong preference for formal legal training (contract law, entertainment and copyright law).

  • In-depth knowledge of all forms of current media, negotiating techniques, corporate business practices, and the funding rules of various agencies including CMF, private funds for screen-based media, provincial agencies across Canada, and tax credit authorities. 

  • Facility with approved artificial intelligence technologies to improve workflow and data analysis. Eagerness to learn and adapt to emerging technologies.

  • Financial and contract management experience. Role includes estimating and validating calculations of tax credits and independent drafting of complex agreements.

  • Strong understanding of linear and streaming entertainment business models, social media, and other online platforms including FAST channels.

  • Strong computer skills including Google suite, Excel, Microsoft Office and Adobe.

  • Ability to comprehend and translate the concerns of creative producers/directors/creative heads into appropriate contracts within the constraints of the applicable regulatory bodies, CBC policies and funding guidelines.

  • Creativity and innovative problem-solving skills to address all policy and production issues in a manner satisfactory to all parties.

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and oral, including an ability to work with both emerging and experienced producers.

  • Ability to handle multiple priorities, and work under pressure.

  • Ability to exercise judgment and work independently taking initiative.

  • Strong analytical skills. 

  • Able and willing to work beyond regular office hours during peak periods of activity as well as the flexibility to attend industry functions and events.

  • Bilingualism (French/English) would be considered an asset.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-09-23 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

This role will be assigned to work shifts including weekends, holidays and overnight.

The opportunity

Function:

Assists in achieving the CBC Radio Canada’s objectives by providing specialized technical and production guidance in the Master Control facility. By undertaking the overall coordination of assigned programs, areas or projects in Digital, Radio and Television. Creative problem solving is required to solve operational difficulties, to assess and optimize the use of resources. Work is generally performed according to accepted CBC or industry standards but there is wide latitude for independent action, judgment and initiative.

Where instructions or requirements are not clear, independent judgments may be necessary under severe time constraints and relevant personnel are contacted for clarification. Problems or faults are reported clearly and promptly to the relevant authority. Receives and replies to audience queries.

Key Tasks:

  • According to Master Control and operational schedules, patches, switches, and routes video and audio feeds and related communications circuits both internally and externally.  Coordinates technical adjustment of these feeds with various production facilities and other clients.
  • Connects temporary facilities for production partners
  • Contributes ideas and makes recommendations to overcome problems or achieve desired results.
  • In accordance with department and program policies, prioritizes and coordinates distribution and collection facilities.  Compiles distribution and collection records for billing purposes.
  • Coordinates routing of feeds, including the booking and purchase of circuits and facilities both domestically and internationally.  Ensures their proper termination.
  • Communicates with common carriers to resolve transmission problems, and with others to distribute information and instructions pertaining to network programming.
  • Checks and verifies the accuracy of Network schedules with those concerned and inserts corrected information.
  • Operates and makes adjustments to ensure proper transmission through distribution and collection systems.  Tests, monitors and reports the response and condition through these systems.  Checks signals meet our plant technical specifications, converts signals as needed including PAL to NTSC and audio manipulation.
  • Receives, coordinates, checks and files program and related information
  • Performs all or part of the function or duties of an equivalent or lower classification.
  • As assigned or required, may perform any or all of the following tasks:
    • Perform tests, measurements and line-ups, and adjust equipment to maintain maximum operating efficiency.
    • Coordinate activities regarding program delivery and presentation.
    • Checks and verifies TV Master Control schedules, inserts corrections and advises of any discrepancies.  Monitors television networks.
    • Sets up and ensures continuity of various communications circuits.

Your role

CBC Yukon has an amazing opportunity in Whitehorse. We’re looking for an experienced journalist to help lead a team that drives local, innovative storytelling on audio, digital, video and social platforms. We’re searching for someone who’s decisive, creative and passionate about everything that makes the Yukon what it is - people, communities, cultures, land, languages, arts, sports, politics and businesses. 

The Yukon is a territory in transition, where there’s space to learn, to experience, to travel, to build a career and a life. 

As a producer assigned primarily to CBC Yukon’s audio-radio shows, your central role is programming our three daily shows, working with dedicated hosts, an associate producer and reporters. You’ll assign, edit and line up segments on Yukon Morning, Midday Cafe and Airplay. You will lead daily team meetings, coordinate story chases, make decisions on audio treatments, write scripts, conduct interviews and coordinate  with News, Digital and Video Producers and reporters across the North and across Canada. 

You will have the opportunity to initiate ideas and projects to engage, serve and grow our audiences by reflecting and amplifying complex Northern stories. There will be latitude for initiative and creativity while adhering to CBC journalistic and/or program policies, standards, and practices. Besides initiating and producing work yourself, there is a regular and ongoing requirement to help coordinate the work of others, within CBC Yukon and with other CBC stations, shows, and hubs.

Working with an editorial leadership team led by CBC Yukon’s Executive Producer, you’ll collaborate with program staff to effectively, efficiently, and empathetically cover stories and issues affecting our diverse audience across the Yukon. Awareness and understanding of local issues and communities across the territory is essential.CBC Yukon also contributes to a N.W.T-Yukon weekend show produced and hosted out of Yellowknife.

Can you see yourself here?

You have a deep and demonstrated understanding of broadcast journalism, responsive, relevant news coverage, digital roll outs and strategic social media storytelling. You’re also keen to consider new ways of telling stories on established and emerging platforms. You understand the role of public media in connecting with and building a strong, flourishing local community. You have experience encouraging and creating content that embraces a diverse range of lived experiences. 

You’re an excellent writer, and all-round communicator. You also have strong vetting skills. You’re insatiably curious, brimming with initiative. You work quickly, thoughtfully and collaboratively. You demonstrate flexibility and adaptability. 

You’re also a confident, compassionate, and inclusive leader. You inspire people to bring out their best. You’ve got experience mentoring, coaching and working alongside a team that brings a broad range of experience, skills and interests. You’re paying attention to what people are talking about and you find ways to bring those voices to the table. You’re open to new ideas and to feedback. 

You’re a great planner and deft organizer who can work in harmony with a small team in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment from pitch, to gathering, to roll out. You are also committed to creating a trusting relationship with our established and emerging audiences by catalyzing, reflecting and responding to Yukon stories in our daily programming. 

You understand our different platforms and how to shape a story to play into each one’s strengths.You’re on the lookout for new ways to connect, including podcasting, on-demand and streaming audio and video.

We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

  • A relevant post-secondary degree or equivalent years of experience.

  • Minimum of 5 years relevant experience of which 3 must involve work in broadcasting or a closely related industry.

  • Strong understanding of the Yukon’s diverse social, political and cultural landscape

  • Demonstrated experience in leading a team or unit.

  • Experience in gathering sound and voices and producing audio segments for radio broadcasts

  • Experience in producing daily current affairs-driven shows 

  • Demonstrated understanding of digital, video and mobile platforms.

  • Superior editorial decision making, critical thinking and listening skills.

  • A thorough knowledge of CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

  • Demonstrated ability to exercise quick, decisive and strong editorial judgment.

  • Highly developed vetting skills.

  • Ability to communicate effectively and cooperatively.

  • Highly developed interpersonal skills.

  • Highly developed organizational skills.

  • Excellent editing/production skills in Dalet and other audio editing software 

  • Ability to work independently and also participate as a member of a production team.

  • A valid driver’s license and a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada’s insurance company


As required, you will perform the following tasks: 

  • Coordinate resources and coverage plans for daily content creation, special projects, series, remote broadcasts and streaming content with a focus on CBC Yukon’s three daily audio shows.

  • Lead story meetings.

  • Participate in the preparation of content for local, regional and national audiences, including assigning, researching, gathering, writing and editing.

  • Write, vet and review scripts and question lines or the shows.

  • Aid in the critical analysis around story selections, treatment and placement, and provide feedback on the same. 

  • Work with hosts to support best delivery and performance 

  • Work with hosts to determine the style, pace, tempo, line-up and format of shows.

  • Frequently contact newsmakers, organizations and community groups to develop a database of ideas for stories and/or programming specials,

  • Provide regular feedback and coaching to experienced and developing journalists. 

  • Ability to work flexible hours and overtime, is required.

CBC News Podcasts is looking for an experienced Producer with a passion for CBC’s news storytelling. This work supports the CBC News Podcasting strategy, which exists to reach new audiences for CBC’s journalism in the podcast and digital audio space.

This is a 12 month temporary, full-time position, Monday to Friday, primarily daytime hours but with flexibility for working with team members coast-to-coast.  It is a hybrid role, requiring you to be in the workplace at least three days a week, at any of CBC locations in Canada. 

About CBC News Podcasts

Canada’s best journalism, on demand and delivered directly into your earholes.

Our mandate is to amplify our news journalism in the podcast space, and that means video and social media are key to our podcasting strategy.

We work with CBC teams in several ways;  

  • producing original always-on news podcasts like Front Burner and Two Blocks from the White House 

  • supporting our local This Is podcasts 

  • assisting network audio and video teams to increase their podcasting presence

  • developing original news podcast series like See You In Court and upcoming investigative series. 

We work in deep collaboration with CBC News Studios, the Podcast Audience Growth Hub, and CBC Podcasts to create audience-focused podcast content and best practices around podcasting.

About the Role:

In this role, you will support our news podcast teams, assigned to new and ongoing projects throughout the year as needed. 

This means you’ll be working with CBC journalists with varying levels of longform audio experience, helping to transform original, enterprise and investigative content into podcast formats that lean into the power of audio storytelling, and will attract new audiences to our work. 

You will be responsible for many aspects of the production process;  reviewing tape, recording and producing interviews, chasing guests, drafting narrative-driven episode outlines, scripts and series arcs, selecting clips, editing audio,  and offering edit notes and suggestions., You will also be responsible for many of the elements needed to help the podcast find new audiences; titles, episode descriptions, promos, trailers and other digital content.  Most importantly, you love working with tape, building scenes and characters and love sharing that knowledge and experience with colleagues at different stages of their podcasting journey.

 

You’re responsible for a variety of tasks, including but not limited to:

  • With oversight from a CBC News Podcasts Exec or Sr or Producer, contribute to the development and production of CBC News Podcast projects as needed 

  • Support CBC News teams in building podcast content from their original, enterprise and investigative journalism

  • Write, produce  and assist in the development of episode and series outlines, interviews, scripts, edit notes, chasing, producing and recording of interviews for a podcast format

  • Gather, record and edit podcast audio from interviews, archival, and news gathered sources.

  • Ensure podcasts are created in accordance with CBC News Podcasts’ strategy and in adherence to the JSP

  • Create podcast growth assets to support our shows and series

About You:

  • You are committed to CBC News’ values around local service, audio strategy, and our Journalistic Standards and Practices

  • You have a track record of producing and writing longform audio storytelling and are passionate about making podcasts

  • You have a minimum of 5 years experience in news media, or podcast production

  • You have experience working with creative contributors, giving feedback and helping others develop skills

  • You’re a creative storyteller who loves to write for the ear, and has a knack for knowing what will sell a story

  • You’re a critical thinker who can come up with innovative ways to use resources to support a wide variety of needs and possible use cases

  • You’re detail-oriented and love to nerd out what small tweaks can make big impacts on content, workflow and audiences 

  • You forge positive team relationships where you value collaboration, transparency, respect and inclusiveness

  • You understand the fundamentals of what makes a podcast different from our other news formats.

Does this sound interesting to you? Please apply with a cover letter that explains why this role with CBC News Podcasts is a fit for you, and include your podcasting CV.

This is a 12 month temporary, full-time position, Monday to Friday, primarily daytime hours but with flexibility for working with team members coast-to-coast. It is a hybrid role, requiring you to be in the workplace at least three days a week, at any of CBC locations in Canada.

Canada’s best journalism, on demand and delivered directly into your earholes.

CBC News has an exciting opportunity for a collaborative team player with  strong editorial judgment, a good understanding of news audience needs, and a knowledge of digital publishing and evolving media platforms. 

We’re hiring a Producer of Client Relations to join our Video Distribution team. The role is to ensure our best-of visual journalism is reaching the widest available audience possible at home and around the world. 

Under the guidance of the Executive Producer, you’ll be overseeing key parts of our daily video inventory as part of our end-to-end distribution of visual content across multiple clients, formats, devices and platforms. 

You’ll be identifying the strongest visuals to share with our external publishing partners, including the European Broadcasting Union, CBS, NBC, CNN and other key clients using our content. You’ll answer requests from partners and provide outlooks so they can see what’s coming.

You’ll work alongside others managing video across CBC News digital properties as we create one cohesive team managing our video together. That includes teams curating video for our news app and web, FAST channels, CBC linear channels, as well as third-party platforms such as YouTube and Tik Tok. 

You’re a collaborator, who builds strong relationships with teams across CBC News and with our publishing partners. In this role, organization, communication, reliability and flexibility are key. 

You are able to pivot quickly to turn breaking news into on-demand video and update as the story evolves. You ensure that content meets the high quality and editorial standards our partners expect from CBC News. An experienced journalist, you’re comfortable making independent editorial decisions in accordance with CBC News Journalistic Standards and Practices. 

You have experience using audience research and performance data to guide your editorial decisions, constantly looking for the story that moves audiences beyond discoverability and into actively engaging with and sharing CBC News video. You search for opportunities to reflect a broad range of perspectives and voices in the content we share. 

You bring a distinctive life experience and expertise to the team. You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for the values of diversity, inclusion and respect in the work culture. 

As someone who embraces change, you are open to exploring new ideas and work processes to support shifting audience behaviour and emerging technologies. You are willing to learn when things don’t go right and from others on your team.  

This position requires you to be on-site at a CBC facility. It’s a Monday-Friday work week. The scheduled hours will be determined based on production needs to support a 24/7 video distribution service. With clients around the world, the hours will likely include early mornings, late evenings and some overtime.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Publish relevant CBC News video to our internal tool, MediaBeach, for pickup by external media clients in Europe, USA and Canada.

  • Act as a daily liaison and maintain relationships with counterparts across CBC News and with media clients.

  • Handle requests for raw and packaged content from external clients. 

  • Verify and clear usage rights for distributing and publishing video content online.

  • Perform Quality Control checks on raw tape and packaged items, including: 

    • Check, identify and flag any rights issues with tape 

    • Check, identify and flag any technical issues 

    • Check, identify and flag issues with supers and on-screen graphics. 

    • Check to ensure correct MetaData. 

  • Co-ordinate with CBC News Resources teams for making live feeds available to partners. 

  • Co-ordinate with other Video Distribution teams to make packaged video available to partners. 

  • Co-ordinate with local regions identifying best-of Canadian content for international audiences. 

  • Populate and maintain outlooks identifying priority video content, creating a menu of available video for clients to choose from.

It aims to become a community hub, diving into local conversations about current events, culture, lifestyle and emerging trends.


To bring this ambitious launch to life, ICI Windsor is seeking a dynamic and engaging Radio Host.


Bringing curiosity, creativity and an innovative spirit to the airwaves, you will host our daily afternoon drive show. Work is governed by CBC/Radio-Canada’s journalistic and programming policies, practices and standards.

  • Knowledge of CBC/Radio-Canada’s mandate and Journalistic Standards and Practices.

These include but not limited to, CBC Ottawa’s Tik Tok and YouTube as well as CBC Ottawa’s news app and website. In the role you will focus on audience growth on digital  platforms and live news coverage on both FAST and terrestrial platforms. 

In your role you are  responsible for text based stories on CBC Ottawa’s website. You are driven by growth and engagement on our digital platforms. You will ensure CBC Ottawa’s web and app presence is responsive, informative and delivers what the audience wants and needs. You lead a video team that thrives on live content on digital platforms, FAST channels and terrestrial broadcast. 

You love data, and you track to assist in making a better audience experience on all platforms. You distribute data to teams to better understand what is resonating with viewers and readers.     

This role is key to moving local news coverage into the future. You are a champion for change and will motivate your teams to get them focused on delivering on mobile-first needs. You work in conjunction with the CBC News’ Audience Growth team to support best practices that set us up to win on mobile and streaming platforms. Reporting to the Executive Producer of News you are part of the CBC Ottawa leadership team and help drive the objectives and mission of the station.

  • Provide and interpret audience data to newsroom leaders to help inform their programming decisions.

  • Provide clear, actionable feedback to teams on audience needs and publishing and packaging fundamentals.

  • Work in partnership with CBC News’ Audience Growth team to:

    • Communicate audience insights and context across all platforms to daily news teams.

    • Establish best practices across platforms to deliver on measurable audience growth goals for CBC News.

    • Optimize high-performing local stories (including photos, graphics headlines, story-framing, sidebars, etc.).

    • Evolve tactics for growing local audiences, including new platform experiments.

  • Increase and develop content that’s driven by a mobile-first lens for CBC’s Ottawa owned and operated platforms on web and app.

  • Champion live and breaking content on all platforms 

  • Oversee video and digital teams 

  • Attend daily editorial meetings and develop assignments through an audience growth lens

  • Ensure current affairs content is being edited for video platforms, including distributed platforms such as YouTube and TikTok.

  • Collaborate closely with the Senior Producer of News to deliver exceptional daily news content that serves the audience 

  • Track and distribute data to enhance audience engagement

  • Build team through training, check-ins, and encouragement 

  • Follow trends in the industry and make recommendations 

  • Work and collaborate with editorial leaders on editorial decisions, specials and planning

  • Ensure visual editorials decision are inline with CBC’s journalistic policies, including verification 

What your bring:

  • Minimum of 5 years newsroom leadership experience 

  • Knowledge of social platforms and broadcast trends that drive audience 

  • A calming influence in the newsroom while making quick decisions

  • Open to team ideas that are outside the box 

  • Knowledge of video crafts both traditional and current 

  • Understand audience habits in streaming, news app and website spaces

  • Desire to increase web traffic through daily and breaking news content

  • Keen understanding of text story structure, headlines and photos that enhance the audience experience 

  • Experience guiding and developing talent, craft and performance

  • Ability to handle multiple priorities while juggling tasks and/or projects

  • Strong analytical skills to solve complex journalistic and operational issues

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills including the ability to be clear, concise, and precise on journalistic and programming matters.

CBC News is looking to hire a senior technology and AI reporter who will help us make sense of this ever important and evolving beat.

We are looking for a smart, energetic reporter who is fully immersed in the news and developments in the technology and AI landscape and has lots of contacts and connections in the industry. Whether it’s a story about how AI is being deployed or how it has changed our lives, you understand the latest trends, where the news is going, and what the impact will be. You’re able to explain this to our audiences on all platforms in an engaging and compelling way. 

As a senior reporter, you are prepared to move fast on breaking news, providing updates as they come and pivoting where required. You are confident going live (and at times, unscripted) on video, radio and on digital live story pages. You have excellent presentation skills and can explain things quickly, simply and accurately on the fly. You work well in a high-pressure, deadline-driven environment. 

You are expected to pitch original stories. You have strong writing, research, and interviewing skills. You are a confident storyteller and can file on-demand pieces in text, audio and video. You craft these stories with a mobile audience in mind. You know how to engage a younger, diverse audience, and are ready to deliver. You are hungry to file stories.

Driven by curiosity and an open, inclusive mindset, you thrive in a breaking news environment and in working collaboratively and effectively with a team. 

This job is 5 days a week, full-time, with an expectation to work overtime and weekends as required. 

This is a permanent full-time position based anywhere in Canada with daily access to a CBC facility. As collaborating with teams across CBC News is a priority, you will be required to be on-site in this role. 

Here’s more details:

Key tasks:

  • Pitch stories about technology and AI that engage our target audience. Break news and follow developments.

  • Go live when the story demands it – and file into live story pages and live programming. Gather news in the field and go on location whenever possible.

  • Cover major or fast-moving events. Work well under pressure.

  • Research, interview and gather new information.

  • Craft work with a target 30-49 diverse Canadian audience in mind. Drive to develop content that will be relevant to this demographic. Make stories relatable to a general audience and explain the impact these stories have on people’s everyday lives.

  • Generate and execute journalism that elevates a range of voices and perspectives.

  • Shape scripts and file stories for all platforms. Prioritize a mobile and streaming audience. 

  • Work collaboratively with editors and vettors to sharpen writing, headlines and text.

  • Understand the elements needed to produce strong visual and audio stories. 

  • Be able to remain calm under pressure. 

  • Recognize issues of importance quickly and take effective action to ensure appropriate coverage. Prioritize demands.

  • Develop and maintain contacts with a variety of sources. Be a leader in the beat and share expertise and knowledge with colleagues.

  • Have a strong understanding of legal journalistic issues and the ethical principles of our Journalistics Standards and Practices. 

  • Work collaboratively with colleagues on the business team and other parts of the CBC.


Your profile:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent. 

  • Minimum 10 years relevant full-time experience. 

  • Excellent understanding of the technology and AI and the impacts they have on our audience. 

  • Come with sources and contacts in the tech and AI community and beyond.

  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the diversity within the tech beat and the diversity of our target audience

  • Experience writing, researching, fact-checking and packaging text, audio and video pieces.

  • Excellent presentation skills; comfortable reporting live and unscripted.

  • Have deep familiarity with social media and have an ability to surface trending stories.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work collaboratively with a team and across departments.

  • Proven ability to work in a high-stress, tight-deadline environment.

  • Experience working on multiple projects simultaneously.

  • Ability to work flexible hours and do overtime as needed.

  • Knowledge of the public broadcaster's role, responsibilities and journalistic standards.

  • University degree in journalism or equivalent preferred.

Please submit a cover letter with your resume, which will be used to help us assess your written communication. Include two examples of each of the following stories: video, audio, text, and live coverage (any format).

Radio-Canada Ottawa-Gatineau is looking for a sporting life videojournalist. This is a permanent, full-time role working three (3) days on a weekday schedule and two (2) days on a weekend schedule.


Your Role  


Reporting to the Senior Digital Producer, Sports, you’ll gather and process news from the local and national sports scene. You’ll be expected to create content for all Radio-Canada platforms. You’ll be responsible for writing copy and producing video for digital platforms as well as contributing to Le Téléjournal Ottawa-Gatineau, live or pre-recorded radio newscasts and programs. You may also be required to work on national programs.


The greater Ottawa-Gatineau area is home to a large number of Canada’s national and multi-sport organizations and professional, college and university sports teams. It offers an extensive range of possibilities for stories about the region’s sporting life, leisure and outdoor activities. This is a unique opportunity to create content that is informative and interesting for our audiences and relevant to their lives. 


Do you have a passion for sports, local sporting life, physical activity and all the accompanying trends? Do you take an inclusive, people-first approach to sports reporting so that your content can be enjoyed by a wider audience including women and diverse communities? Do you have a network of contacts in the sporting world on both the Ottawa and Gatineau sides of the region or has your past experience demonstrated your ability to develop and maintain sources? Do you like to propose original stories while staying up to date on what’s happening every day? Then this position is for you!


You must be able to work independently, have excellent organizational skills, be highly creative and possess sound editorial judgment. You’ll prepare, align, set up and operate various cameras and ancillary equipment, ensuring optimal audio and video quality under prevailing conditions. Work is governed by CBC/Radio-Canada programming policies and Journalistic Standards and Practices. When needed, you may be asked to lend a hand in the newsroom as a general news videojournalist.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


What you bring:

  • Graduation from university or community college in a relevant course of study.
  • Minimum of three (3) years’ relevant journalism experience.
  • Solid reporting skills.
  • Proven skills shooting and editing video to tell compelling stories.
  • Comfortable and dynamic on-air presence.
  • Excellent interviewing skills.
  • Ability to write clearly and concisely.
  • Flexibility to work regularly for television, radio and/or digital platforms.
  • Creative problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of the latest sporting events as well as sports-related community and socio-economic issues.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the key issues facing Ontario, Eastern Ontario and the Ottawa/Gatineau region.
  • Demonstrated range of visual storytelling techniques and digital best practices.
  • Strong knowledge of social media and digital platforms in general.
  • Critical acumen.
  • Proven ability to generate original story ideas and knowledgeable contacts.
  • Strong desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.
  • Proven conversational writing style.
  • Ability to respond to breaking news situations quickly and accurately.
  • Ability to work independently as well as in teams.
  • Ability to work flexible hours in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment, often in unexpected overtime situations.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Solid command of French and good knowledge of English (asset).
  • Valid driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada’s insurer.
  • Valid passport and ability to travel as needed.
  • Knowledge of camera models Sony PXW x200, Sony RX10 and Sony A7R iv is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Avid Media Composer, Photoshop and Lightroom is an asset.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

 

Please note this is an on-call position.

 

Your Role


We are seeking stagehands to prepare, set up, install, assemble, tear down, load, unload and transport scenic elements, operate stage machinery and scenic equipment, and handle hands-on production tasks. Stagehands also prepare and configure filming locations to meet production requirements.

 

Key Tasks:

  • Prepare, position, install, assemble, strike, load, unload, transport, move and rearrange scenic elements according to instructions to meet production needs; procure scenic elements as required.
  • Read plans, drawings and instructions to build and strike sets and scenic elements accordingly.
  • Set up, install, adjust, operate and dismantle equipment (such as camera tracks and dollies) according to instructions; procure required equipment and materials as needed.
  • Install and operate stage machinery and scenic equipment according to instructions to fulfil production requirements.
  • Connect various equipment and props as directed, check their operation and report any issues.
  • Operate forklifts, aerial platforms and other motorized vehicles to transport materials or access equipment for installations and adjustments; perform routine maintenance and report servicing needs to the appropriate department.
  • Perform basic cooking, food preparation and beverage service as requested for production needs.
  • Handle and manage cue cards and prompt sheets as directed.
  • Dismantle scenic elements according to instructions, salvaging and preserving reusable materials.
  • Mark and spike rehearsal areas in accordance with plans and instructions.
  • Assist in rigging scenic elements onto battens or other supports, and help establish safety perimeters during installations and manoeuvres.
  • Maintain clean, orderly and well-kept work areas, filming locations and scenic elements.
  • Touch up paint and carry out minor repairs on set elements as needed to fix damage or imperfections.
  • Set up dressing rooms, makeup areas and related furniture and props as needed.
  • Prepare location sites (including setting up wheelchair ramps, guardrails and scaffolding, and levelling ground) to address spatial and production constraints.
  • Keep studio doors closed to maintain a controlled production environment within the studio and surrounding areas.
  • Adhere to rules in effect and guidelines when bringing or moving motorized vehicles and live animals on set.
  • Adjust, modify, repair and maintain scenic elements.
  • Receive, tag and store scenic equipment and materials and update inventory records; report missing or damaged items to the appropriate department and follow up as required; assist with regular inventory counts.
  • Ship, deliver and pick up scenic equipment and materials as directed, logging all incoming and outgoing inventory.
  • Inform staff of the availability and stock location of scenic equipment and materials.
  • Inspect returned equipment and materials for completeness and proper operation; take necessary corrective action and follow up as needed; report any damage or defects to the appropriate department.
  • Weigh scenic equipment and materials to determine loads for rigging or transport, reporting figures as required.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; share information verbally or in writing to ensure proper followup and to keep others informed.
  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and the work environment.
  • Carry out, as needed, all or part of the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

 

Job Requirements:

  • High-school diploma.
  • Twelve (12) months' relevant experience required to perform the duties satisfactorily, given that training is not directly or indirectly related to the job and given the variety of tasks involved (e.g., assembling sets during overnight shifts, working with furniture and props, working on live sets, working outdoors during galas).

Your role:

CBC News Operations is looking for a Supervising Technician to support our production personnel in the field. In this position you will have various responsibilities including: purchasing of equipment, management of our internal database, basic equipment maintenance, technical support and troubleshooting (remote and on location), equipment co-ordination, training, technical writing and researching new equipment. You will be a central point of contact for all our domestic and foreign bureau staff.

As the Supervising Technician, you provide specialized technical and production guidance, by leading employees, and by undertaking the overall coordination of assigned programs, areas or projects in Audio and Video. Creative problem solving is required to solve operational difficulties, to assess and optimize the use of resources, and to motivate others. The ability to act quickly, while remaining calm under pressure in a fast paced, deadline driven environment is a must. 

Key Tasks:

- Maintains familiarity with technical or production installations and any associated equipment.

- Conducts surveys and prepares detailed reports.

- Acting as a consultant, provides assistance and advice on operational requirements in terms of equipment, facilities and personnel and procedures, creates, edits and produces written documentation on equipment and workflows.

- Within delegated limits, plans, assigns, schedules, coordinates and checks the work of assigned staff and reports on matters related to job performance, conduct and safety.

- Trains new staff and advises management on their progress. Arranges training.

- Verifies the accuracy of time reports and work performed.

- Undertakes reviews of the operations, operating procedures, technical standards and maintenance activities. Submits recommendations for improvements or modifications.

- Recommends safety procedures. Plans and maintains safety measures and programs for personnel, property and equipment.

- Reviews, investigates and verifies reports and institutes any action as necessary.

- Within delegated authority and in consultation with the supervisor:

- Commits the Corporation in arranging, with outside persons or firms, for the provision of supplies or services

- Reviews or directs such arrangements

- Verifies delivery of material or completion of service.

- As assigned or required, may perform any or all of the following tasks:

- Within delegated limits, hire staff for casual requirements

- Provide specialized assistance and work in close consultation with Engineers and Technologists

- Provide input to the budget process.

- Participate in the selection and evaluation of new staff.

- Performs all or part of the function or duties of equivalent or lower classifications.

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

- Community college graduation in Radio or Television arts courses, or equivalent industry experience.

- Minimum 4 years directly related experience.

- Requires a superior knowledge and understanding of radio or television program production and presentation methods. This includes understanding how different areas interrelate.

- Valid standard full Driver’s Licence required

- Knowledge of Video Processing and Transcoding, Computer Hardware and Networking, SNG and transmission technology is a bonus.

CBC News is looking for an innovative and versatile video producer with a strong interest in world news and excellent field video producing skills to join our new bureau in Jerusalem, covering the Middle East. If you’re a creator at heart and enjoy storytelling and producing content across visual formats, this job could be for you. 

At a time when the world, and Canada’s place within it, is rapidly changing, being present on the ground to bring stories Canadians want and need to know about is critical. As part of our expanding world coverage team, you’ll work closely with a correspondent in Jerusalem, your colleagues in other world bureaus and journalists with Radio-Canada, who will also be working in the Jerusalem bureau. 

You bring a deep knowledge of the historical complexities of the Middle East and the confidence to help shape the CBC News editorial coverage. 

You’re a technical whiz who will be shooting, editing, packaging and publishing content using a variety of gear and apps. This includes social video content, live hits, live streams and on demand content. 

You are also strong editorially. You have story ideas and are thinking about creative treatments to attract new and younger audiences through social-first formats. You excel at guiding stories from concept to post-production, and are quick to pivot when plans change. 

You are deeply committed to the values of a public service broadcaster. You uphold the CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices, especially our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality and integrity. 

You understand that stories can break at any time of the day and you have a genuine desire to be on-top of that coverage. The position requires long-hours, flexible schedules and a willingness to deploy on a moment’s notice, including to conflict zones. The minimum assignment length for this position is two years and, if agreed to by both parties, may be extended for up to an additional two years. 

What you’ll be doing: 

  • Pitches, shoots, produces and edits short and long-form digital-first video content tailored for platforms like TikTok and YouTube as well as CBC.ca.

  • Manage on-the-ground gear — including cameras, portable lighting, and wireless mics — to capture visually impactful footage and clean audio for news content. 

  • Ingest, organize, assemble, and edit raw footage into compelling narrative formats using industry-standard software (such as Premiere Pro); attention to good sound design and mixing; knowledge of basic motion graphics/titles to elevate production value. 

  • Generate and execute compelling journalism, including researching, writing, generating and editing video, audio and text. 

  • Performing location surveys and identifying special requirements such as audio, lighting, camera angles and equipment, including production limitations. 

  • Providing technical guidance and expertise focused on content production techniques, workflows and creative content gathering techniques for complex situations. 

  • Collaborate effectively across CBC News to ensure comprehensive coverage across multiple platforms, programs and locations. 

What is required: 

  • You are a seasoned video-journalist with at least five (5) years of directly related field experience at a network/national level and, preferably in a foreign environment, who thrives in a deadline driven, high pressure environment. 

  • A superior level of technical knowledge and understanding of live coverage, social treatments, visual gathering, visual production and post-production methods and remote filing tools.

  • A strong sense of creativity, initiative and a high degree of responsibility for the accuracy and quality of work throughout the complete production cycle.

  • Demonstrated editorial skills, showing proficiency in story preparation and production of highly creative, innovative visual storytelling, from story generation through to the final edits. 

  • Strong communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills are required, including active listening, problem-solving and an ability to work across teams.  

  • Ability to work independently in a deadline-driven environment while maintaining a professional attitude.

  • Must possess a valid passport and have the ability and willingness to travel internationally on short notice. 

  • Graduate degree/diploma from a University or Community college in a relevant course of study or equivalent industry experience. 

  • Ability and willingness to work overtime and various shift patterns including overnights and weekends. 

Your application will be evaluated on your experience, as well as your portfolio of work. 

Please include at least two examples of: 

  • Digital / social stories you produced and shot

  • Packaged daily news video content you shot and edited 

  • A cover letter that tells us why you want this role, and how you will use your experience to support the bureau
