job.title: Marketing and Operations Executive, SEA
job.description:
We are looking for a dynamic and experienced Marketing and Operations Executive to join the International Marketing team at Sony Music. In this role, you will build, implement and improve the processes, technology and data of the International Marketing team in South East Asia; providing planning, governance and insights to enable the team to focus on the creative process, operate efficiently and deliver value to the region and the artists.

What you'll do:

  • Guide the marketing reporting strategy to ensure the marketing team has timely, accurate and relevant data and insights to build, execute and monitor campaigns.
  • Lead the collation, reporting and tracking of data from DSPs and other platforms, produce insights, and build and maintain reports to share with the broader marketing team on a weekly basis.
  • Define relevant KPIs to track performance by DSP and other relevant platforms, at the territory and aggregate level.
  • Interrogate data and use it to identify trends and propose actions to the wider marketing team and other stakeholders when relevant.
  • Lead post- campaign analysis to determine campaign performance and determine lessons learned and actionable insights for future marketing efforts.
  • Enhance campaign operations and marketing processes across International Marketing by standardising best practices, automating workflows, and improving collaboration between local and regional teams.
  • Actively participate in campaign planning activities, including but not limited to defining the marketing objectives for each campaign, creating and managing project plans with clearly defined deliverables and resources, defining success criteria and KPIs and providing insights to inform campaign activities.
  • Coordinate workstreams and dependencies, track and communicate progress, identify obstacles, and ensure they’re addressed.
  • Ensure marketing campaigns are executed according to the agreed plan and budget, and flag potential risks and issues on time.
  • Optimize international marketing processes in the region to enable the team to grow, scale and deliver the expected revenue.
  • Work with the broader marketing team and finance to define campaign budgets and manage the day-to-day tracking of marketing budget spend across all teams.
  • Work with the wider marketing team to support critical activities through a set of standard marketing reports (weekly, monthly, quarterly and by half year).

Who you are:

Experience in marketing, marketing ops/program management in a creative industry, including building and optimizing processes and systems.  Know how on global release procedures and processes.
Practical creative experience such as videography/filming and editing/photography/animation/design - a plus but not essential. 

Well-versed of SEA markets music culture and it’s customer behaviours.

Technical capabilities:

  • Storytelling: Ability to build a solid narrative for the artist, including core identity and backstory, brand, semiotics, image, visuals, and translate that into tangible marketing and fan experience and engagement actions
  • Data Literacy: Ability to analyse the music market and relevant data and apply insights to make decisions to drive / improve results. Able to review assets against established ingest and metadata guidelines and processes.
  • Project Management: Ability to plan and organise internal and external resources to deliver the agreed outcomes for a variety of projects within the agreed quality timeframe and budget.
  • Digital literacy: Thorough understanding of how the various technologies that drive music consumption work and how to use them to create content and drive audience / fan engagement.  

Behavioral capabilities:

  • Agility: Responds and adapts quickly to changes, maintaining a flexible attitude and using the new conditions to evolve their thinking.
  • Creativity: Ability to generate new and useful ideas and to execute them through a variety of media and digital and non-digital platforms.
  • Problem Solving: Has a "can-do" attitude and sees obstacles as opportunities to find alternative ways to do things and grow, demonstrating resourcefulness and flexibility.
  • Communication: Ability to articulate an idea or point of view verbally or in writing succinctly, with clarity and confidence, adapting the message to different audiences.
  • Operational excellence: Ability to proactively determine opportunities for improvement and optimising processes and technology to achieve business’ goals.
  • Cultural awareness: Understand popular culture and the underlying cultural patterns and factors that influence behaviours in different teams and countries.

job.title: Merchandise Lead, Finance Supervisor - GFFS
job.description:
At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time. Today, we work in more than 60 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

The Global Finance Shared Service Center supports the core business with finance related matters, covering a wide scope of activities across the globe. We ensure suppliers and artists are paid on time for the amazing work they create. We work closely with the local finance teams around the world, which means we have an excellent understanding of how the company operates and are kept up to date with key developments in this exciting and fast-paced industry. Our teams play a key role in ensuring Sony Music achieve their annual goals each year.

As our Global Finance Shared Service (GFSS), you will be overseeing the following USA merchandise business areas: 

  • Accuracy of the accounting entries made by GFSS across tour, e-commerce, and licensing revenue streams
  • Accountability for the output of our Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) partner.
  • Be the primary GFSS contact for other GFSS departments, and the merchandise and label finance or sales teams.

This role requires a highly organized, confident, motivated team player who operates well under pressure.

It is a role for someone equally comfortable designing a process and executing one.

What You'll Do:

Accounting Integrity — Merchandise Business

  • Own the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting within GFSS’ scope across all merchandise revenue streams. Including revenue recognition, cost of sales, vendor obligations, and balance sheet positions
  • Act as the accounting lead to ensure proper accounting for unusual scenarios
  • Review and approve all reconciliations, reports, and financial summaries before they are sent to other departments and stakeholders
  • Maintain a thorough working knowledge of how each merchandise revenue stream flows through SAP so that accounting positions can be taken and explained or justified
  • Ensure the accounting is structured to withstand external, statutory, and artist audits at any point

Process Design and Problem Solving

  • Identify gaps in current accounting workflows and develop approaches to address them
  • Implement process changes/improvements and ensure they are documented, repeatable, and scalable

Vendor Payables and Cost Accounting

  • Maintain accounting for vendor cost obligations arising from merchandise operations, including venue revenue-sharing arrangements
  • Ensure accrued payables are recorded correctly, cleared on a timely basis, and the balance is kept clean
  • Coordinate with Accounts Payable (A/P) to ensure vendor payments are applied correctly in SAP and the payables ledger reflects the true state of outstanding obligations

US State Sales Tax Reporting

  • Support the US sales tax compliance process with Sony Global Tax Office. g. state filings, and timely settlement of tax liabilities.
  • Review supporting data, reconciliations, and schedules required for filings

Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Team Management

  • Directly manage the offshore Team Lead. Set clear performance expectations, review output quality, and develop the team’s capability over time
  • Hold accountability for the performance of the offshore team supporting Merchandise — the standard of work that reaches GFSS management and stakeholders is this role’s responsibility

Stakeholder Management

  • Serve as the primary GFSS accounting contact for merchandise and label finance, accounts payable, and senior management
  • Work directly with the merchandise sales and operations team to understand how the business operates and translate that into accounting solutions and proper documentation
  • Take on increasing responsibility for direct customer-facing communication as the function matures
  • Ensure issues are escalated proactively

Who You Are:

  • Degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA, CA, or equivalent professional designation
  • 5-8 years of progressive accounting experience, including direct management of a team; public accounting professionals transitioning to industry are encouraged to apply
  • SAP (S/4HANA) experience preferred across A/R, G/L modules, along with general knowledge of the A/P module
  • Sound working knowledge of IFRS 15 applied to a multi-stream revenue business
  • Demonstrated experience with sales tax compliance is an asset for this role
  • Reliable track record managing a remote offshore team to a high standard of output quality is a plus
  • Excellent written and spoken English; this role communicates regularly with senior management
  • Experience in entertainment, music, live events, or merchandise is an asset. Intellectual curiosity about the industry matters equally

What We Give You:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day  
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.

job.title: Optimization Manager
job.description:
Optimization Manager is responsible for driving digital revenue growth across streaming platforms (DSPs) such as Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, and other digital partners. This role focuses on managing platform relationships, optimizing commercial opportunities, and maximizing the performance of the company’s music catalogue and releases across digital services. 

 

What you will do:

  • Manage and grow relationships with key Digital Service Providers (DSPs) including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, TikTok, and others.
  • Develop and execute digital sales strategies to maximize streaming revenue and platform monetization. 
  • Identify and secure editorial placements, playlists, and promotional opportunities with DSP partners.
  • Monitor and analyze streaming performance, revenue trends, and platform insights.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, A&R, and Audience Development teams to align release strategies with DSP opportunities.
  • Drive revenue growth through campaigns, platform partnerships, and commercial initiatives.
  • Negotiate and execute commercial deals and partnerships with digital platforms.
  • Prepare regular performance reports and insights for internal stakeholders.
  • Track industry trends, platform updates, and competitor activities.

 

Who you are:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Management, or related field.
  • Minimum 5–7 years of experience in growth / digital sales / strategic partnerships / business development.
  • Experience in the music industry would be an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of Indonesia’s music streaming ecosystem (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, etc.).
  • Proven experience in revenue growth & digital monetization.
  • Strong analytical skills with ability to transform streaming and sales data into business action plan.
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and work effectively in a fast-paced and highly collaborative environment. 
  • Basic understanding of music and the Indonesian music industry, including familiarity with Indonesian artists, Indo songs, and Indo genres.

 

What we give you 

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to fuel the creative journey 
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork 
  • We invest in your professional growth & development 
  • An excellent range of benefits, like private medical cover, life assurance, etc. 

 

Equal Opportunities

As an active part of a culturally and socially diverse society, Sony Music’s aim is that our workforce is diverse and inclusive. Sony Music is an equal opportunity employer and supports workforce diversity.

job.title: OTC - Open Talent Pool
job.description:
If you’re interested in future opportunities within our OTC (Order to Cash) team, we invite you to apply to our OTC Talent Pool by submitting your CV through this application. This allows us to stay connected and reach out when suitable OTC roles become available within our Global Finance Shared Services (GFSS) team in Warsaw.

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. From being home to the world’s first music label to shaping the future of music, entertainment, and technology, we’ve played a pioneering role in music history. Today, we operate in more than 60 countries, supporting a diverse roster of global superstars, independent artists, and visionary creators. Across everything we do, we are driven by creativity, collaboration, transparency, and entrepreneurial thinking.

Our Global Finance Shared Services Centre plays a vital role in supporting Sony Music’s core business worldwide. The team delivers end‑to‑end finance services across a wide scope of activities, ensuring suppliers and artists are paid accurately and on time for the incredible work they create. By partnering closely with local finance teams across the globe, GFSS has a strong understanding of how the business operates and contributes directly to Sony Music achieving its annual goals.

As part of the OTC talent pool, you may be considered for future opportunities in the OTC team. This team are primarily responsible for supporting financial postings & accruals; various accounting and sales reporting reconciliations; invoicing across various territories; overseeing cash application and receivables management; as well as other special projects as directed by management. 

The GFSS team is based in our modern workspace at the Elektrownia Powiśle centre in Warsaw.

If you’re looking to grow your career in finance within a global, creative, and fast‑paced organisation, we’d love to hear from you. 

What you'll do:

Financial Posting, Accruals, and Cash Application

  • Review financial postings, accruals, and General Ledger (GL) and Accounts Receivable account reconciliations to ensure they are accurately and timely reported as requested by Local and Global Management
  • Invoicing of deal partners per sales reporting or contractual terms & review of manual journal entries.
  • Intercompany invoicing.
  • Supervision of allocation of cash payments received against the corresponding agreements
  • Proactively monitoring JIRA & Cadency systems and escalating aged items for resolution.
  • Ad Hoc tasks as required.

Special Projects 

  • Special Projects & Transformation Initiatives - Support
  • Business Process Improvements
  • Suggest and drive system changes to improve daily processes
 Communication & Coordination 
  • Ongoing interaction & communication of issues with management, affiliates, and team members
  • Liaise & coordinate with various teams on joint work items.
  • Act as an emergency contact point for European affiliates and coordinate necessary actions for time zone specific items.
  • Team meetings -setting sessions, and monitoring the progress of completion of assigned projects/tasks.
  • Updating KPIs slides with appropriate comments

Who you are:

  • Bachelor’s degree; Accounting/Finance preferred
  • Relevant work experience
  • Detail oriented individual with strong organizational and leadership skills
  • Ability to balance multiple tasks simultaneously and manage time productively
  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written
  • Comfortable sharing ideas and speaking up
  • Team player with experience working in a multinational environment
  • Ability to analyze and review information from several sources (corporate systems)
  • Prior experience with SAP and Business Warehouse would be strongly preferred
  • Capable of working independently, while also integrating into a team environment
  • Solid understanding of Microsoft Office applications, especially Excel
  • Proficiency in Polish and English language required: reading, written, and oral
What we give you:
  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day 
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community 
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next

job.title: Product Manager
job.description:
As a Product Manager, you'll play a central role in bringing Sony Music artists and releases to market. Working across a diverse roster of local and international talent, you'll lead the planning and execution of release campaigns, helping artists connect with fans and achieve commercial success across physical and digital channels.

Partnering closely with artists, managers and internal teams across Marketing, Digital, Sales, A&R and Operations, you'll develop innovative campaigns, oversee release strategy, manage budgets, and identify opportunities to grow audiences, engagement and revenue. This is a fast-paced, highly collaborative role for someone who combines creativity, commercial thinking and a passion for music.

What You'll Do

Marketing Strategy

  • Develop and deliver release strategies, marketing campaigns, and artist development plans.
  • Forecast project performance and oversee marketing activity from planning through to release.
  • Manage contracts, invoices, and project administration.

Media Promotion

  • Build strong relationships with media partners to maximise artist visibility.
  • Coordinate interviews, appearances, fan events, and other promotional opportunities.
  • Oversee the creation of advertising and promotional materials.

Social Media & Content Strategy

  • Partner with the Digital Marketing team to create content and social campaigns that grow audiences and engagement.
  • Support campaigns across streaming, social, and digital platforms.

Physical Sales

  • Coordinate physical releases with artists, managers, A&R, Sales, and Operations teams.
  • Create sales materials and retail tools to support commercial success.

Digital Sales

  • Work with Digital Sales teams to deliver campaigns across DSPs, social platforms, and digital partners.
  • Identify opportunities to increase streams, reach, and revenue.

Internal Systems & Operations

  • Manage release set-up, asset delivery, and metadata across internal systems.
  • Partner with Operations to ensure releases are delivered accurately and on time.

Reporting

  • Share regular marketing, sales, and campaign performance updates with stakeholders and artist teams.

Marketing Budget Management

  • Develop and manage marketing budgets aligned to release objectives.
  • Track spend and ensure campaigns are delivered within budget.

Who You Are

  • Experience in the music industry across marketing, promotions, publicity, digital marketing, events, or artist development.
  • Strong understanding of social media, digital platforms, and music consumption trends.
  • Confident using Microsoft Office, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook.
  • Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • A creative thinker with a strategic mindset and focus on results.
  • Flexible and willing to travel for artist activity, events, content shoots, and campaigns.
  • Passionate about music, culture, and connecting artists with fans.

 

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day 
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community 
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next 
  • We give you the platform to champion positive change, with the opportunity to contribute to our social impact, diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives 
  • We provide an excellent range of benefits like private medical cover, a generous pension scheme, life assurance, income protection, plus loads of music industry perks. There’s also time off over winter break

job.title: Royalties - Open Talent Pool
job.description:
If you’re interested in future opportunities within our Royalties teams, we invite you to apply to our Royalties Talent Pool by submitting your CV through this application. This allows us to stay connected and reach out when suitable Royalties roles become available within our Global Finance Shared Services (GFSS) team in Warsaw.

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. From being home to the world’s first music label to shaping the future of music, entertainment, and technology, we’ve played a pioneering role in music history. Today, we operate in more than 60 countries, supporting a diverse roster of global superstars, independent artists, and visionary creators. Across everything we do, we are driven by creativity, collaboration, transparency, and entrepreneurial thinking.

Our Global Finance Shared Services Centre plays a vital role in supporting Sony Music’s core business worldwide. The team delivers end‑to‑end finance services across a wide scope of activities, ensuring suppliers and artists are paid accurately and on time for the incredible work they create. By partnering closely with local finance teams across the globe, GFSS has a strong understanding of how the business operates and contributes directly to Sony Music achieving its annual goals.

As part of the Royalties talent pool, you may be considered for future opportunities in one of our two Royalty teams; Royalty Operations or Royalty Accounting. In our Royalty Operations team, you will be a key contributor to the day-to-day operations within Royalties and will be involved in all aspects of artist royalties, managing and delivering accurate and timely royalty statements, performing reviews, analysis and reconciliations, managing and prioritizing clearing of suspense items, responding to internal and external inquiries, contract interpretation, coding and special projects. In Royalty Accounting, you will be responsible for all aspects of royalty accounting for designated affiliates, ensuring the accuracy and completeness of accounting closes, performing account analysis and reconciliation, and royalty reporting.  You will work closely with all areas of the royalty department, corporate, global reporting and planning and external auditors.

The GFSS team is based in our modern workspace at the Elektrownia Powiśle centre in Warsaw.

If you’re looking to grow your career in finance within a global, creative, and fast‑paced organisation, we’d love to hear from you.

 

What you'll do as a Royalties Accountant:

  • Prepare, review and analyze capitalized balances, associated royalty payables, recoupable recording and marketing costs, for reasonableness and proper accounting treatment.  Prepare label talent provision and marketing recovery journal entries
  • Review foreign royalty expense and prepare monthly accrual vs. actual analysis, intercompany reconciliations and associated journal entries
  • Perform various balance sheet account analysis related to artist, copyright, union and foreign royalties to substantiate balances and clear reconciling items.  This includes any royalty system to general ledger reconciliations
  • Monitor, review and analyze artist/copyright/union expense for reasonableness and proper accounting treatment.  Prepare manual journal entries to adjust royalty expense
  • Special projects/other duties as assigned by management
  • Review and improve internal controls where applicable

What you'll do as a Royalties Operations Analyst:

Royalty Contract Interpretation and Coding:

  • Read the artist, producer, and/or third-party contract to obtain relevant information.
  • Interpret contractual clauses related to the royalty obligation, including understanding the legal definitions of terms used within the contracts or related documents.
  • Coordinate with Label’s legal and business affairs staff to obtain missing information.
  • Set up and maintain accurate contractual information within the royalty system

Royalty Statement Review:

  • Prepare the appropriate accounting statements as contractually required,
  • Review sales and costs to ensure they are accurately stated.
  • Update and analyze unrecouped balance analysis at account level.
  • Prepare and research variance-reporting analysis to understand fluctuations with balances and payments.

Sales & Suspense Management:

  • Review the new release schedule and work with the affiliate personal to ensure new releases are coded within the appropriate timeframe.
  • Run sales query and reviewing results with Manager.
  • Prepare and review suspense reports and provide reports to affiliate on a weekly basis.

Inquiries & Special Projects:

  • Serve as Point of Contact for various internal and external inquiries related to assigned accounts.
  • Provide Manager with status reports regarding the assigned artist accounts.
  • Provide guidance to the entry-level staff members including providing an overview of tools available to assist in the completion of the assigned tasks.
  • Assist in process design improvements focused on enhancing quality while reducing resource requirements.

Who you are: 

  • Bachelor’s Degree, preferably in Business Administration, Economics, Accounting or Finance
  • Relevant work experience
  • Strong proficiency in Word, Excel (Pivot tables & VLOOKUP) and Outlook; SAP, EROS, and JIRA experience a plus
  • Detail oriented individual with strong organizational and leadership skills that can handle multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to interact well with different levels within the organization.
  • Ability to analyze and review information from several different sources (corporate systems). 
  • Polish and English language, written and oral
  What we give you:
  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day 
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community 
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next 
  • We give you the platform to champion positive change, with the opportunity to contribute to our social impact, diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives 
  • We provide an excellent range of benefits like private medical cover, a generous pension scheme, life assurance, income protection, plus loads of music industry perks. There’s also time off over winter break

job.title: Senior Business Solutions Specialist - PDEGO
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

About Business Solutions

Business Solutions partners with our label, marketing, and release planning teams to build the tools and workflows that help them run more effectively. We operate as a trusted internal partner, not an order-taking function. Our work is guided by three principles: Fail Fast: test ideas quickly, and don't let perfection get in the way of progress; Learn Quickly: treat every iteration as a chance to learn, document, and adapt; and Move Forward: keep the work, and the people we support, moving.

Role Summary

The Senior Business Solutions Specialist is the trusted day-to-day partner for a dedicated portfolio of business units spanning US and international markets, owning the full solution lifecycle from discovery through delivery, while mentoring the broader NYC Specialist team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for your assigned business units
  • Run discovery, scoping, and requirements-gathering sessions independently
  • Build and maintain business systems, automations, and workflows supporting label, marketing, and release operations
  • Write specs and requirements for integrations with internal Sony Music systems
  • Lead data migrations for assigned business units
  • Test solutions with end users and incorporate feedback quickly
  • Share best practices with the broader team, contributing repeatable patterns and playbook content to support other junior Specialists
  • Escalate architecture/platform-level questions to the Architect
  • Identify opportunities to centralize and standardize workflows across assigned BUs
  • Lead enablement and change-adoption efforts within your portfolio – training business users to use AI tools (e.g., Claude Cowork) to solve their own recurring problems, not just handing off finished solutions
  • Define success metrics for initiatives in your portfolio and use adoption/usage data to evaluate outcomes and guide iteration
  • Ensure initiatives align with governance, privacy, security, and compliance requirements, partnering with the Architect and relevant stakeholders (Legal, InfoSec) as needed


Required Qualifications

  • 5-8+ years in business/systems analysis, solutions consulting, or enterprise no-code/low-code platform administration, with the judgment to build solutions that are secure, scalable, and well-governed
  • Demonstrated ability to run point independently with senior business stakeholders
  • Strong requirements-gathering, process-mapping, and documentation skills
  • Experience with data migrations
  • Comfortable managing multiple concurrent projects and business units
  • Extensive A.I. experience using tools such as Claude Cowork, ChatGPT Work, Google Gemini
  • Basic scripting, SQL, or automation-logic familiarity
  • Tool-agnostic and adaptable to learning new platforms as workflows expand
  • Experience leading change adoption or user enablement efforts within a business function
  • Comfortable defining measures of success and using data to evaluate outcomes


Nice to Have (not required)

  • Music industry experience; media & entertainment adjacency (rights, royalties, metadata) a plus
  • Airtable certification or deep hands-on Airtable expertise (our current core platform)

A Note on Applying

  • We encourage you to apply even if you don't check every box

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day  
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.  
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next  
  • Time off for a winter recess

Sony Music is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, veteran or military status, marital and civil partnership/union status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

The anticipated annual base salary does not include any other compensation components or other benefits that an individual may be eligible for.  The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include as applicable, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.New York Pay Range$125,000—$140,000 USDThe anticipated annual base salary does not include any other compensation components or other benefits that an individual may be eligible for.  The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include as applicable, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.California Pay Range$125,000—$140,000 USD

job.title: Senior Coordinator, Corporate Communications & Publicity - The Orchard
job.description:
About The Orchard

The Orchard is a leading global music distributor and Artist & Label services company operating in 50+ markets worldwide. The Orchard empowers creators and businesses to grow and adapt in the dynamic global music industry. We specialize in being artist focused, blending industry expertise and technology, leveraging data to drive success, and providing streamlined digital and physical distribution solutions. The Orchard’s comprehensive artist & label services offerings include marketing, sync licensing, premium video services, transparent data analysis, advertising, rights management, radio promotion, D2C, and more.

The Orchard focuses on providing a comfortable, social, and engaging environment to encourage productivity and creativity.

The Orchard is seeking an experienced and clever communicator to join our global Corporate Communications team. The Senior Coordinator, Corporate Communications and Publicity will lead strategies that enhance The Orchard’s public profile and key messaging via an informed, amplified voice in media including press coverage, industry events, speaking engagements, as well as internal communications and client-focused initiatives. The role is essential to enhancing the communications department goals and coordinating with other departments to ensure overall brand visibility. The Senior Coordinator, Corporate Communications is a full-time, in-office position based in New York City at The Orchard’s headquarters and reports to the VP Global Corporate Communications.

What you'll do:

  • Office- first role, in office 4 days a week.
  • Aid in the planning and execution of communications initiatives that support The Orchard’s internal and external strategic priorities
  • Assist in drafting press materials, including releases, bios, talking points, decks as necessary
  • Collaborate with departments company-wide, assuring clear, consistent, and compelling messaging 
  • Maintain close relationship with umbrella corporate communications department; uphold and enforce guidelines
  • Perform department admin duties such as invoices, press tracking, face sheets, guest lists, and more
  • Hire and direct photographers as necessary; Service photographs to media 
  • Compile and distribute weekly and semi-annual media reports for leadership
  • Manage company-wide approvals for all speaking engagements
  • Maintain Comms calendar with speaking events, artist performances, social events, trade shows, awards shows, and other appropriate opportunities for company leadership 
  • Maintain and organize departmental resources and records including annual subscriptions, press database, photos, bios, media mentions, and more
  • Adopt and implement new technology initiatives including daily news circulation, media briefs, and more
  • Compile targeted media lists as directed by the department lead; maintain journalist beats and moves
  • Collaborate with the Director of Media & Artist Relations to support publicity campaigns and media outreach for select artists across The Orchard's roster
  • Track and submit information/submissions for industry power lists 
  • Collaborate with external media partners
  • Monitor client nominations and wins at global awards ceremonies
  • Identify story ideas aligning with company goals and select client initiatives
  • Elevate internal and external company events, coordinate conference participation
  • Identify and evaluate music industry-related data including trends, current events, hot topics, etc. 
  • Attend company events and shows

Who you are:

  • 2+ years of music industry corporate communications or publicity experience, preferably at a label or independent PR firm
  • Strong understanding of the music media and PR landscape; understanding of digital distribution preferred
  • Some established relationships with reporters, editors, social media influencers, photographers, and cultural tastemakers
  • Experience executing press campaigns

job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Alamo Records, Santa Anna Label Group, Foundation Media, and OVO Sound operate across a fast-moving, rapidly growing portfolio of labels, joint ventures, distribution partners, and artist deals. We are looking for a strategic, commercially minded Senior Director of Finance & Accounting who understands the broader label business and can support decisions around artists, joint ventures, acquisitions, catalog, cash flow, and profitability with insightful analysis. The ideal candidate will bring deep accounting expertise, strong operational discipline, and exceptional analytical and financial modeling skills.

In the near term, this person, in coordination with SME central teams, will provide hands-on leadership to strengthen accounting practices, including intercompany accounting, financial operations, and metadata management, to ensure accurate and comprehensive reporting. The Senior Director of Finance & Accounting will also be responsible for the monthly close and forecast, as well as the annual budgeting process. As part of a small, flat team supported by the wider Sony Music Finance, Accounting, and IT infrastructure, this person will touch virtually every aspect of label finance and accounting. The role requires someone who navigate a complex organizational structure and bring the technical accounting expertise the group needs.  This will require taking ownership of detailed project management and process design and execution.  Through this work, the Senior Director of Finance will build the experience and perspective needed to grow into a future CFO-level leader for the organization.

What you'll do:

  • Lead accounting setup, cleanup, and ongoing financial control processes across Alamo, Santa Anna, Foundation, OVO, and related ventures, with particular focus on entity structure, intercompany accounting, eliminations, reconciliations, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Strengthen accounting controls, workflows, and ownership across recurring close, reporting, intercompany, and operational finance processes.
  • Oversee monthly close, management reporting, variance analysis, balance sheet reviews, and corporate deliverables, ensuring results are accurate, timely, and clearly explained to senior management and SME stakeholders.
  • Manage annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, and long-range planning across labels, joint ventures, acquisitions, and new business initiatives, connecting financial plans to operating priorities, deal terms, and profitability targets.
  • Partner with SME central teams, including Accounting, Global Finance, Tax, Royalties, JV Accounting, Metadata, and technology partners, to improve financial operations, data quality, metadata workflows, systems integration, and reporting consistency across a complex organizational structure.
  • Support deal analysis, artist and label investment decisions, catalog and acquisition opportunities, royalty and recoupment analysis, and new venture business plans, ensuring financial assumptions align with contractual terms and operational realities.
  • Act as a senior finance business partner to label leadership and department team members across business units to help drive revenue growth, profitability, cash discipline, and operating efficiency all the business.
  • Serve as a reliable #2 to the CFO, leading detailed project management, integration efforts, process improvement initiatives, and other high-priority finance projects as a hands-on operator and strategic finance leader.

Who you are:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting or Finance required.
  • 10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, ideally within music, media, entertainment, or another complex multi-entity environment.
  • CPA strongly preferred; MBA a plus.
  • Passionate about music, media, and entertainment.
  • Deep technical accounting foundation, including a strong understanding of month-end close processes, balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, eliminations, and intercompany accounting across multiple legal entities.
  • Strong financial planning, forecasting, modeling, and analysis skills, with the ability to translate detailed financial data and analysis into clear recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Sophisticated Excel skills, with the ability to analyze and interpret large data sets.
  • Analytical mindset with a natural desire to ask “why,” coupled with the initiative to reimagine and reinvent processes and improve the accuracy of reporting and analysis.
  • Experience working with corporate accounting, tax, royalties, metadata, systems, and shared service teams to resolve cross-functional issues and improve end-to-end financial operations.
  • Hands-on leader with a roll-up-your-sleeves attitude, high attention to detail, and the ability to manage complex projects at a granular level.

job.title: Senior Manager, Audience Intelligence
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

The Senior Manager, Audience Intelligence leads Sony Music Canada’s audience insights function, delivering data-driven intelligence that informs campaign planning, audience growth, fan engagement, and direct-to-consumer strategy across the organization. The position currently manages 1 direct report and reports into a broader regional team spanning the U.S, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

This role focuses on transforming audience, streaming, social, and commerce data into actionable insights that support artist development, release strategy, CRM initiatives, and fan monetization opportunities.

The Senior Manager plays a critical role in measuring release and campaign performance, uncovering audience trends, to build a more unified view of the fan journey from streaming discovery and social engagement through to owned-channel interaction and commerce conversion.

This is a highly collaborative role for an analytically driven individual who is passionate about music, fan behaviour, and the evolving music data and distribution ecosystem.

What you'll do:

Analytics & Audience Insight Development

• Collaborate with Commercial Partnerships, Marketing, A&R, the Executive team and Audience Intelligence teams with real-time insights to inform artist signings, campaign planning, optimization, and post-campaign analysis.
• Collect, analyze, and interpret audience data across streaming platforms, physical sales, social media, paid media, CRM, and D2C commerce channels.
• Conduct deep-dive analyses into audience behavior, fan demographics, psychographics, and engagement trends to support targeting and segmentation strategies.
• Identify emerging audience opportunities, cultural trends, and high value fan segments that can inform artist marketing and growth strategies.
• Manage product release forecasting and audience trend analysis for domestic and international frontline and catalogue priorities.
• Deliver ad-hoc analysis to support the needs of the business, assist with other projects and process improvement initiatives as required.

D2C, CRM & Fan Lifecycle Intelligence

• Lead audience measurement and performance reporting across Sony Music Canada’s direct-to-consumer ecosystem, CRM programs, and owned fan acquisition initiatives.
• Analyze customer behavior, conversion trends, retention, and purchase activity to inform D2C strategy and optimization.
• Develop frameworks that map audience pathways between streaming engagement, social interaction, CRM acquisition, and commerce conversion.
• Partner with digital and marketing teams, and D2C stakeholders to identify opportunities for fan acquisition, audience re-engagement, lifecycle marketing, and conversion growth.

Reporting, Visualization & Operational Excellence

• Build and evolve scalable dashboards, KPI scorecards, and reporting frameworks tracking campaign performance, audience growth, streaming trends, CRM engagement, and D2C performance.
• Translate complex datasets into clear, actionable business intelligence for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Assist with funding requests (e.g., Ontario Music Investment Fund), support new business development, and handle ad hoc data or reporting requests from key departments.

Who you are:

• 5+ years of experience in analytics, digital marketing, audience insights, or performance reporting (music, entertainment, media, or e-commerce preferred).
• Proficiency in analytical languages such as SQL and/or Python is considered a strong asset.
• Experience with analytics and BI tools including Alteryx, Tableau, Power BI and Shopify analytics.
• Experience with music and audience platforms including Luminate, Spotify for Artists, Apple Music For Artists, Amazon Music For Artists, YouTube Analytics and Chartmetric.
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills with experience working across multiple datasets.

job.description:

Reporting to Director, Global Total Rewards, with a dotted line to the VP, Payroll, you will be the subject matter expert for payroll, working closely with the wider generalist teams and finance teams to ensure data is accurately inputted, processed, approved and reported on a monthly and annual basis.  You will be responsible for the relationship with our external payroll provider as well as leading on all payroll projects.

What you'll do:

Payroll Strategy and Vendor Management

Working closely with the wider PX generalist and Finance teams, ensuring data is accurately inputted, processed, approved and reported each pay period. job.title: Sr. Director, Digital Development - Columbia
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

The Senior Director, Digital Development at Columbia Records builds the viral foundation for projects before they scale. Where the wider Viral Marketing team drives influencer campaigns at volume around established artists and priority singles, this role sits at the front end: developing artists, first singles, early-stage projects, and catalog titles showing early signals of movement.

The work is diagnostic, strategic, and hands-on. Read the audience quickly, map the niches that matter, find and test the content that actually works inside them, and run point on the seeding that puts it in front of the right communities. Once a project has traction and a proven approach, it transitions to a Viral Marketing lead to scale further. The role sits within the Viral Marketing team at Columbia Records and works alongside Marketing, Audience and Social teams from project kickoff.

What you'll do:

  • Own the viral strategy for developing artists and early-stage projects, from pre-release through the first signs of traction, before campaigns move into scaled execution.
  • Build a fast, accurate read on each project’s audience: who they are, where they sit online, what they already engage with, and what the artist’s credible entry point is.
  • Map and pressure-test the niches and creator communities around a project (subcultures, formats, sounds, references) and identify where the artist has real cultural permission to land.
  • Identify and test content angles inside those niches at low cost and high frequency. Prove what works before budget scales.
  • Run point on seeding strategy and execution for early-stage projects: set the seeding plan, choose the communities and accounts, brief the content, and place it. This is hands-on work, not oversight.
  • Build and maintain the seeding infrastructure the front end of a campaign depends on: page networks, community accounts, creator relationships, and the process for moving content through them quickly.
  • Establish the creative foundation each campaign scales from: the hook, the format, the angle, the seeding logic, documented clearly enough for the wider Viral team to run with it.
  • Work closely with the Catalog and Legacy divisions to surface titles showing early signals of growth, and build viral strategies around them fast enough to catch the moment.
  • Monitor catalog and recent releases for emergent movement (UGC velocity, sound usage, search and DSP behavior, playlist and platform signals) and flag opportunities proactively rather than reactively.
  • Partner with Marketing, Audience and Social from kickoff so viral strategy is built into the campaign, not bolted on afterward.
  • Build early relationships with creators and micro-communities relevant to developing projects, where fit matters more than reach.
  • Transition proven projects to the Viral Marketing leads with a clear strategy, evidence of what works, and the seeding and community groundwork in place.
  • Report findings, tests, and results to senior staff, translating early signal into recommendations the wider team can act on.

Who you are:

  • 7+ years professional experience in influencer, social, or digital marketing, with significant time spent on early-stage artists, emerging brands, or projects built without an existing audience.
  • Hands-on seeding experience: has personally built and run seeding operations, not only directed them. Familiar with page networks, community accounts, and the mechanics of placing content at speed.
  • Track record of setting strategy that other teams execute, and of influencing senior stakeholders across departments without direct authority over them.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and build inside niche online communities, not only mainstream creator channels.
  • Strong instinct for internet culture paired with the research discipline to back it up. Fluent across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and the adjacent platforms where subcultures form.
  • Experience testing content and reading results quickly. Comfortable being wrong fast and adjusting.
  • Working knowledge of streaming and consumption data, DSP behavior, and third-party trend tools.
  • Genuine knowledge of music history and catalog, and real interest in why older records find new audiences.
  • In-depth knowledge of music culture, trends, and creator communities.
  • Clear written communication. This role produces the strategy that others scale.
  • Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity, able to move on projects that do not yet have structure around them.
  • Experience mentoring or developing junior team members, with the judgment to build process where it is needed and leave it out where it is not.
  • Experience with AI tools to accelerate research and streamline workflow where appropriate.
 

What we give you:

  • You join an inclusive, collaborative and global community where you have the opportunity to channel your passion every day  
  • A modern office environment designed to foster productivity, creativity, and teamwork empowering you to bring your best 
  • An attractive and comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life & disability coverage, and 401K + employer matching 
  • Voluntary benefits like company-paid identity theft protection and resources for pets, mental health and meditation resources, industry-leading fertility coverage, fully paid leave for childbirth or bonding, fully paid leave for caregivers, programs for loved ones with developmental disabilities and neurodiversity, subsidized back-up child and elder care, and reimbursement for adoption, surrogacy, tuition, and student loans 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.  
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt, and create what happens next  
  • Time off for a winter recess

The Vice President, People Experience (PX) Business Partner, West Coast owns the strategy, leadership and delivery of the PX agenda for our West Coast business units, approx. 350+ employees across the labels and corporate teams anchored in our Los Angeles office. You are the senior PX voice in the market: trusted partner to the CEO, COO and label/BU Presidents, and the leader who turns their business plans into a coherent, best-in-class employee experiences across the full employee journey.

This is a strategy and a delivery role. You set direction in partnership with the Americas and Global PX leadership, and you lead a team of two to three PX Business Partners to execute it. The Orchard is a leading full-service music distribution company operating in 50+ markets worldwide and servicing top global independent artists and labels. With cutting-edge operations and an unparalleled global team, The Orchard partners with clients to provide full scale solutions across a variety of verticals. Championed by an exceptional community of music lovers and experts, The Orchard empowers creators to grow and evolve in the dynamic, global industry. 

The Orchard focuses on providing a comfortable, social, and engaging environment to encourage productivity and creativity.

The VP, Catalog is an entrepreneurial leader and growth operator responsible for the vision, structure, and revenue growth of the Global Catalog Division. This role moves beyond traditional maintenance to treat the company’s entire repertoire across all lifecycle stages as a dynamic, high growth engine.  Reporting to the SVP, Commerce, this executive operates as a key leader within the company's organizational framework, ensuring catalog priorities are seamlessly integrated into label business planning and coordinated across territories, Relationship Management, and Services teams. Leading a high-performing team including a Senior Director and a Director, this leader ensures the existing repertoire is positioned for cultural resurgence, algorithmic dominance, and sustained global P&L growth.

What You'll Do:

  • Global Strategy & Market Growth: Build and own the Global Catalog roadmap in partnership with the SVP, establishing the operating protocols and KPIs that shift the organizational mindset toward total repertoire value. Ensure catalog priorities are fully integrated into label business planning and cross-functionally coordinated across global territories, Relationship Management, and Services teams.
  • Commercial P&L & Multi-Pillar Execution: Assume full accountability for the Catalog division’s financial health and revenue targets. job.title: VP, D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy (Fan Engagement)
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing artists, songwriters, producers, and creators. Across our business, we are building the next generation of music commerce, fan engagement, and direct-to-consumer experiences globally.

The Role

Sony Music is seeking a VP, D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy to join the global Sony Music D2C organization. Reporting directly to the Head of Sony Music D2C, this role will lead the D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy team within The Greenhouse, Sony Music’s centralized D2C division.

The purpose of this team is to make D2C marketing a constant, evergreen discipline for labels that today focus their effort on the release cycle. It is a central, cross-label team that acts as an extension of label digital marketing and international market execution — providing D2C expertise, filling execution capacity gaps, and building the frameworks that let others work well — while leaving artist narrative and campaign strategy with the label.

This is deliberately a small centre rather than a large production function. Labels resource their own D2C people for their own repertoire; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that unlock the value those teams create. Where a label does not yet have that capability, the team carries more of the work early and steps back as the label staffs up. There is no embedded headcount — the team operates as a shared service across labels and territories.

The VP is accountable for the quality and commercial performance of D2C creative, product and campaign activity across the roster, and for the relationships that make it work: with label marketing, creative and commerce teams, with the international marketing team, and with partners across The Greenhouse. Much of the work is proposing rather than deciding — the label approves throughout — which makes credibility, judgement and influence without authority central to the role.

The role leads a team of five to six, organised around three pillars: creative, covering design systems, production and D2C visual standards; product, covering D2C product management, pricing and lifecycle; and campaign, covering CRM, fan acquisition and marketing operations. The ideal candidate combines strong D2C product instincts, fan marketing expertise, creative sensibility and operational rigour, with a deep understanding of how fans engage with artists, music, merchandise and culture across global markets.

How This Team Operates

  • A small centre, not a production house. Labels resource their own D2C people; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that let them create value.
  • Proposes rather than decides. Recommendations are put to the label for approval. The team holds no authority independent of the label, and labels retain final say on every D2C decision.
  • Reuses and refines rather than originates. Artist narrative and campaign concept sit with the label. The team adapts existing creative for D2C — merchandise creative is the one area where it originates.
  • Depth varies by situation. On a frontline release the team is advisory. Between release cycles, on evergreen catalog, it is the primary owner of D2C activity with label approval. On superstar campaigns it is fully engaged alongside label and international teams.
  • Depth also tapers by label. Heavier engagement early where D2C capability is thin, lighter as the label staffs up — every label lands in the same place.
  • Always-on, not campaign-by-campaign. Label marketing works per release; international marketing works per market, per release. This team spans releases and keeps D2C running between them.

What You’ll Do

Creative

  • Build the D2C design system — templates, asset taxonomies and scalable creative frameworks that let labels and territories execute high-quality D2C creative at volume across markets.
  • Establish D2C visual and email standards, including motion templates, content hierarchy, build quality and testing practice, with labels supplying artist voice and brand direction.
  • Produce merchandise and D2C product creative that labels do not produce in-house — pack shots, product mockups, banners and bundle imagery.
  • Produce D2C social assets and CRM builds when label teams lack the capacity, and refine or extend existing creative for D2C where core assets are limited.
  • Create pitch decks and D2C creative concepts that help label teams sell campaign ideas internally and to artist teams.
  • Resolve international asset adaptation, where D2C creative differs meaningfully by territory and is today handled late and inconsistently.
  • Supply campaign creative and merchandising direction to the Store Experience team, who build and run the storefronts.

Product

  • Establish the process linking D2C with marketing, sales and merchandising — the coordination gap labels consistently identify as their biggest constraint, where marketing learns of product and release decisions too late to build a proper campaign.
  • Develop D2C product insight across bundles, exclusives, premium formats and drops, proposed to the label for approval.
  • Own D2C pricing and promotional recommendations across markets, with label approval and international input from the commercial strategy team.
  • Run competitor scanning, launch retrospectives and evergreen product ideation, bringing trend and net-new format thinking to label and commerce teams.
  • Build lifecycle and scarcity frameworks — pre-order windows, limited editions, flash drops, live-show tie-ins, gated access and evergreen replenishment.
  • Ensure D2C approaches are globally consistent where scale matters and locally adapted where fan behaviour, language, pricing, territory, chart rules or fulfilment realities require it.
  • Partner with operations on launch readiness, product setup and localisation, and supply demand signals into the forecasting and insights team.

Campaign, CRM & Marketing Operations

  • Train label teams to think D2C natively — what assets are needed, at what cadence, and which products fit which moments.
  • Build the D2C campaign cadence, framework and schedule that keeps label campaigns on track — a named gap where no one currently owns the rhythm of D2C activity across a release.
  • Own domestic D2C CRM and lifecycle marketing across the full fan journey — email, SMS and owned channels — including automated journeys that keep fans engaged between release moments, not only campaign sends.
  • Develop a fan segmentation framework spanning casual fans, active fans and superfans, enabling more personalised communication and experiences across every channel.
  • Build the first-party data strategy that captures fan preferences and behaviours to create richer fan profiles, and own domestic fan acquisition.
  • Provide D2C budget deployment and retargeting guidance, developed with the label.
  • Create D2C paid media best-practice frameworks across Meta, TikTok and Google, with clear guidance on campaign structure, audience strategy and measurement. D2C performance marketing is a distinct discipline from awareness and engagement advertising and is not resourced consistently across labels today.
  • Define flywheel analytics, channel health standards and reporting — tracking acquisition, engagement, retention and monetisation, and how fans move from streaming, social and owned properties into D2C channels.
  • Establish best practice for loyalty and VIP programmes that reward engagement rather than purchase alone, social commerce integrations, and creator and affiliate partnerships — with labels executing against those standards.
  • Advise label teams on preorder strategy, launch timing, segmentation, local market messaging and campaign optimisation, and drive a test-and-learn culture across creative and messaging.
  • Over time, develop predictive audience modelling to identify high-value fans and churn risk, and prepare the design system and asset taxonomy for AI-assisted asset generation.

Partnership & Interlock

  • Serve as the central D2C creative, product and campaign partner to labels, artist teams and territories — including Columbia, RCA, Epic and the UK — and to Ceremony of Roses, The Orchard and merchandise partners.
  • Define and operate the interlock with the international marketing team, who own market localisation and in-territory execution for US repertoire. This role owns the domestic equivalent and sets the global standard; the handoff between the two requires clear, agreed triggers.
  • Work across The Greenhouse with the Store Experience, Business Operations, Commercial Strategy and Customer Satisfaction functions, whose scope adjoins this team’s at multiple points.
  • Build the relationships and credibility to influence without authority across a highly matrixed global organisation.

Who You Are

  • 10+ years across fan engagement, D2C marketing, CRM, eCommerce, merchandising or digital marketing in a high-volume, multi-stakeholder environment; music or entertainment experience strongly preferred.
  • Deep understanding of music fan behaviour, artist marketing, D2C commerce and fan engagement ecosystems.
  • Track record of enabling distributed teams — building playbooks, standards and frameworks that others execute — rather than only running work centrally. Comfortable moving between doing the work and teaching it.
  • Able to operate through influence rather than authority, and to build the trust that makes label teams want to work with a central function.
  • Strong knowledge of lifecycle marketing, CRM platforms, email and SMS execution, segmentation and first-party data strategy. Familiarity with Shopify ecosystems and D2C storefront operations.
  • Practical experience with D2C performance marketing — paid media planning, audience targeting and return on ad spend — or the judgement to build that capability.
  • Strong creative instincts and experience collaborating across design, marketing, merchandising and product functions, with the credibility to work alongside label creative teams.
  • Experience building scalable campaign workflows, design systems and operational best practice in high-volume environments.
  • Global mindset and sensitivity to local market nuance — fan behaviour, pricing, language, cultural context, release priorities, chart rules and fulfilment realities.
  • Passion for music, fandom, culture and evolving consumer experiences.

What We Give You

  • An opportunity to shape the future of global music commerce and fan engagement at scale.
  • Collaboration with industry-leading artists, labels and entertainment executives.
  • A dynamic and entrepreneurial culture within one of the world’s leading entertainment companies.
  • Investment in professional growth and long-term career development.
  • Competitive compensation package including salary, bonus eligibility, comprehensive benefits and additional Sony Music perks.

Sony Music is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, veteran or military status, marital and civil partnership/union status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

job.title: YouTube Channel Strategy Manager - The Orchard

We are seeking a motivated, forward thinking, and dynamic YouTube Channel Strategist to join our UK team. Ideally you will have experience advising artist and label clients on Youtube strategy.

This position reports to the Director, Channel Strategy, with project direction from Relationship Manager Lead. The role serves as the dedicated manager for a roster of YouTube channel partners.

The ideal candidate is relationship driven, both creative and analytical, and comfortable working proactively and autonomously.

The Orchard teams meet in the London, Kings Cross office between Monday-Thursday. Fridays are spent working remotely.

What you'll do:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for artists, labels, and Relationship Managers across an assigned roster of priority channels.
  • Maintain consistent and effective communication with internal teams and external partners.
  • Execute strategic post launch initiatives across marketing, optimization, and growth activities to maximize reach, retention, revenue, and overall client satisfaction within a high touch service model.
  • Provide ongoing, hands on support including programming, optimization, analysis, reporting, content strategy, marketing support, and troubleshooting.
  • Deliver exceptional service for MCN clients and internal teams (Relationship Managers, Rights Management, Operations, and others) to ensure video related issues are resolved quickly and accurately.
  • Conduct detailed channel and video audits with actionable recommendations and implementation plans.
  • Track, analyze, and report on channel and category performance using metrics such as CPM, viewership trends, and audience demographics.
  • Collaborate with Relationship Managers, Marketing, and Audience Development to leverage YouTube for key campaigns and to develop platform specific initiatives for priority artists and labels.
  • Partner closely with the Director of Channel Strategy to communicate partner issues and roadblocks and ensure seamless post launch account management.
  • Maintain accurate and up to date records across internal systems, YouTube CMS, and YouTube.com.
  • Provide best practice guidance and tailored strategic recommendations to assigned clients.

Who you are:

  • Deep understanding of the digital ecosystem and the ability to leverage platforms such as user generated content and social media to achieve goals.

  • Technically savvy, comfortable with data, and proficient in YouTube CMS, Microsoft applications, Google Workspace, and Apple applications.
  • Familiarity with Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Premiere, Illustrator, and After Effects.

We're looking for a Senior Director, Integrated Marketing & Growth to oversee SoundCloud's growth marketing ecosystem and connect every customer touchpoint into a unified engine that drives acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, monetization, and advocacy. job.title: Advertising Operations Specialist – Retail Media
job.description:
Department Operations Location Montreal

At Stingray, creativity, collaboration, and innovative technology are at the core of our DNA. Are you ready to rock your career by joining a fast-growing company and a team of music enthusiasts in a stimulating and fun work environment? 

Stingray is a leading global music, media, and technology company. We provide curated musical and video content to businesses and consumers on a variety of platforms, including digital television, OTT, mobile, and in-store media solutions. Our mission is to connect people through the power of music.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and technically skilled Ad Ops Specialist to join our growing Advertising Operations team. This role will focus on the end-to-end management of audio advertising campaigns within the rapidly expanding Retail Media landscape. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in digital ad operations, a passion for the audio advertising ecosystem, and experience working with retail media networks. You will be responsible for ensuring the flawless execution, delivery, and optimization of our clients’ audio campaigns.

Your day-to-day

  • Campaign Management: Manage all aspects of audio ad campaigns from setup to completion, including trafficking, testing, and launching campaigns in our ad serving platforms (e.g., Hivestack).
  • Retail Media Focus: Serve as the subject matter expert for audio advertising on Retail Media Networks (RMNs), understanding the unique technical requirements and opportunities.
  • Trafficking & QA: Implement and test ad creative.
  • Proactively troubleshoot and resolve any technical issues.
  • Performance Monitoring: Continuously monitor campaign pacing, performance, and delivery to ensure KPIs are met. Identify opportunities for optimization and provide recommendations to the sales and account management teams.
  • Reporting & Analysis: Generate and deliver regular campaign performance reports for internal stakeholders and clients. Provide insights and analysis on campaign results to inform future strategies.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with Sales, Account Management, and external partners to ensure campaign objectives are understood and executed correctly. Provide technical support and guidance throughout the campaign lifecycle.
  • Inventory Management: Assist in forecasting and managing audio ad inventory to maximize revenue and yield.

Your qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Technology, or a related field.
  • 2-4 years of experience in digital advertising operations, with a preference for experience in audio advertising.
  • Hands-on experience with major ad servers and platforms (e.g., Hivestack, Google Ad Manager, Triton Digital’s Tap, AdsWizz).
  • Demonstrated understanding of the digital advertising ecosystem, including, ad-serving logic, and programmatic advertising.
  • Experience with or strong knowledge of Retail Media Networks and their advertising capabilities is highly desirable.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and provide actionable insights.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and problem-solving abilities.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team-based environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.

Life at Stingray
